name: vscode-firebird-studio
description: Firebird Studio — explore, query, and manage Firebird databases directly inside VS Code.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Browsing and querying your own saved connections works in an untrusted folder. Two things are withheld until you trust it: connections declared by the folder's .vscode/firebird.json (which could point at a server someone else chose, and prompt you for a password to reach it), and any workspace-set path for the external isql, gbak and docker programs this extension runs.

firebird.codeCompletion.keywords.description: Enable code completion for Firebird-specific keywords.

firebird.codeCompletion.database.description: Enable code completion for Firebird Database table and field names.

firebird.useNativeDriver.markdownDescription: [Experimental] Use native driver instead of the node based driver *Needs to have FireBird installed* (required for WireCrypt support)

firebird.enableConnectionPooling.markdownDescription: Keep idle connections open and reuse them for subsequent queries instead of reconnecting every time, improving performance on repeated queries against the same database.

firebird.connectionPool.maxSize.markdownDescription: Maximum number of idle connections retained per saved connection when `#firebird.enableConnectionPooling#` is on.

firebird.connectionPool.idleTimeoutMs.markdownDescription: How long (in milliseconds) an idle pooled connection is kept before being closed, when `#firebird.enableConnectionPooling#` is on.

firebird.profiler.pollIntervalMs.markdownDescription: How often (in milliseconds) the Live Profiler re-polls connection activity while its panel is open and visible.

enumDescriptions: Use the driver's default (Read Committed, No Record Version).
Read Committed: see the latest committed version of a row a concurrent transaction is updating, instead of waiting on or conflicting with it.
Read Committed: wait on (or conflict with) a concurrent transaction updating a row, instead of reading its prior committed version.
Snapshot (Concurrency): the whole transaction sees a consistent snapshot of the database as of its start.
Snapshot Table Stability (Consistency): like Snapshot, but takes a protected lock on every table it touches.
firebird.transaction.isolationLevel.markdownDescription: Transaction isolation level for every query/batch Firebird Studio runs. Leave empty to use the driver's own default.

firebird.transaction.lockTimeoutSec.markdownDescription: Lock wait timeout, in seconds, before a query blocked on a row/table lock gives up (`0` = wait indefinitely, Firebird's default). Only honored by the pure-JS driver (`firebird.useNativeDriver: false`) — the native driver's transaction API has no equivalent numeric option, only wait/no-wait (see `firebird.transaction.waitMode`).

firebird.transaction.readOnly.markdownDescription: Open every query's transaction as READ ONLY, rejecting any statement that tries to modify data.

enumDescriptions: Wait for a conflicting lock to clear, optionally bounded by firebird.transaction.lockTimeoutSec.
Fail immediately instead of waiting for a conflicting lock.
firebird.transaction.waitMode.markdownDescription: Whether a query that hits a lock conflict waits or fails immediately.

firebird.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Registers the **Firebird MCP Server**, exposing whichever connections have `firebird.database.toggleMcpExposure` turned on as read-only schema-inspection tools (`list_connections`, `get_schema`) to any MCP-compatible AI client. No connection is exposed by default even when this is on — each one needs its own explicit opt-in from its right-click menu. Requires a VS Code build with MCP server registration support; has no effect on older versions.

enumDescriptions: Open query results in an editor group, beside the SQL file.
Dock query results in VS Code's bottom Panel, alongside Terminal and Problems, leaving the editor full width.
firebird.queryResultsLocation.markdownDescription: Where **Query Results** open, mirroring vscode-mssql's `mssql.openQueryResultsInTabByDefault`. Changing this affects the next query you run; a results view already open stays where it is.

firebird.messagesDefaultOpen.markdownDescription: Open the **Messages** tab, rather than the first statement's results, after running a batch. Mirrors vscode-mssql's `mssql.messagesDefaultOpen`. Messages is always available either way; this only decides which tab you land on.

firebird.messagesIncludeTimestamps.markdownDescription: Include each statement's clock time when using **Copy All** in the Messages pane. The pane always shows the times on screen — this is only about what lands on the clipboard.

firebird.resultsFontSize.markdownDescription: Font size (in px) for the **Query Results** grid, mirroring vscode-mssql's `mssql.resultsFontSize`. `0` uses the webview's own default size.

firebird.resultsFontFamily.markdownDescription: Font family for the **Query Results** grid, mirroring vscode-mssql's `mssql.resultsFontFamily`. Empty uses the webview's own default font.

firebird.shortcuts.markdownDescription:
Keyboard shortcuts for actions inside the **Query Results** webview (grid editing, freeze column, copy selection as SQL) — mirroring vscode-mssql's `mssql.shortcuts`. These only take effect while a result grid has focus, and use `ctrlcmd`/`+`-joined combo syntax (e.g. `"ctrlcmd+alt+i"`, where `ctrlcmd` means Ctrl on Windows/Linux and Cmd on macOS), not VS Code's own keybindings.json syntax. Omitted keys keep their default combo; set a key to `""` to disable it. Available keys and their defaults:
- `event.toggleEditing`: `ctrlcmd+alt+g`
- `event.addRow`: `ctrlcmd+alt+n`
- `event.applyChanges`: `ctrlcmd+alt+s`
- `event.toggleFreezeColumn`: `ctrlcmd+alt+z`
- `event.copyAsInsert`: `ctrlcmd+alt+i`
- `event.copyAsInClause`: `ctrlcmd+alt+k`

firebird.isqlPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `isql` or `isql-fb` executable used by **Connect with ISQL** / **Run File with ISQL**. Leave empty to search `PATH` automatically.

firebird.gbakPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `gbak` executable used by **Backup Database** / **Restore Database**. Leave empty to search `PATH` automatically.

firebird.showSystemObjects.description: Show a 'System Tables' folder listing Firebird's built-in RDB$ system/metadata tables under each database.

firebird.dockerPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `docker` executable, used by **Add New Connection**'s Docker option to auto-detect running Firebird containers. Leave empty to search `PATH` automatically.

firebird.logLevel.description: Logging level in the output channel.

firebird.maxResultRows.description: Maximum number of rows a query result will show. 'Select All Records' asks the server for at most this many (a FIRST clause), and any larger result is trimmed before it reaches the results view, which says so when it happens. Use 0 for no limit.

firebird.maxTablesCount.description: The maximum table count shown in the tree view. Use 0 to show all tables.

firebird.maxRecentConnections.description: The maximum number of recent connections to display at the top of the connection picker.

enumDescriptions: New SQL editors open with no connection bound — you must pick one explicitly.
New SQL editors inherit the connection from the previously active editor (default, preserves existing behaviour).
New SQL editors automatically connect using the connection specified in firebird.defaultConnectionId.
firebird.newEditorConnectionBehavior.markdownDescription: Controls which connection a newly opened `.sql` editor gets. Mirrors `mssql.newEditorConnectionBehavior`.

firebird.defaultConnectionId.markdownDescription: The saved-connection ID to auto-apply when `#firebird.newEditorConnectionBehavior#` is set to `defaultConnection`. Copy the ID from the connection tree's right-click menu.

firebird.recordsPerPage.description: Number of records per page to show in results view.

firebird.linting.enabled.description: Enable SQL linting for Firebird SQL documents.

firebird.linting.missingWhereWarning.description: Warn when UPDATE or DELETE statements are missing a WHERE clause.

firebird.linting.validateTableNames.description: Validate table names against the active database schema.

firebird.quickQueries.markdownDescription:
Saved SQL queries bound to the `firebird.quickQuery.1` … `firebird.quickQuery.9` commands **by position** — the first entry is Quick Query 1, the second is Quick Query 2, and so on. These ship with no default keybindings on purpose: assign your own in VS Code's Keyboard Shortcuts editor (search for "Firebird: Run Quick Query"). Mirrors vscode-mssql's Quick Queries.

Each entry takes:
- `sql` (required): the SQL to run. May contain `${selectedText}`, replaced with the editor's current selection — e.g. `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ${selectedText}` over a highlighted table name. A query using the placeholder with nothing selected is refused rather than run.
- `name` (optional): shown in messages; defaults to the query's first line.
- `action` (optional): `run` (default) executes immediately, `open` puts the SQL in a new editor for review first.

A bookmark can also claim a slot (**Assign to Quick Query Slot** in the Bookmarks view); an entry here wins over a bookmark for the same slot.

name.description: Display name; defaults to the query's first line.

action.description: 'run' executes immediately; 'open' puts the SQL in a new editor instead.

enumDescriptions: Uppercase every keyword Firebird Studio recognises (SELECT, FROM, LEFT JOIN, ...).
Leave keywords exactly as they were typed, and only change layout.
firebird.format.keywordCase.description: How SQL keywords are cased when a .sql file or notebook cell is formatted. Indentation is not set here -- formatting follows the editor's own indentation (editor.tabSize / editor.insertSpaces) so that a formatted file matches what the editor is already showing.

languageModelTools.name: firebird_listConnections
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the Firebird connections saved in this workspace.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the Firebird connections available in this VS Code workspace, with the connection id every other Firebird tool needs. Never includes credentials. The writeEnabled field tells you upfront whether firebird_runWriteQuery is permitted for a connection. Call this first when you don't already have a connection id.

languageModelTools.name: firebird_getSchema
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read a Firebird database's tables, columns, primary keys, and foreign keys.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the schema (tables, columns, primary keys, and foreign keys) of one Firebird connection as JSON. Use this before writing SQL against a database you haven't inspected yet. Firebird dialect notes: identifiers created unquoted are folded to uppercase; row limiting uses FIRST n SKIP m or OFFSET/FETCH, never LIMIT; system metadata lives in RDB$-prefixed tables.

connectionId.description: A connection id returned by firebird_listConnections.

languageModelTools.name: firebird_runQuery
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run a read-only SELECT against a Firebird database.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Executes a single read-only SELECT (or WITH ... AS (...) SELECT) statement against a Firebird connection and returns the rows as JSON. Any other statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL/EXECUTE BLOCK) or more than one statement is rejected — this tool is read-only; use firebird_runWriteQuery for a write. Firebird uses FIRST n SKIP m or OFFSET/FETCH rather than LIMIT.

connectionId.description: A connection id returned by firebird_listConnections.

languageModelTools.name: firebird_getQueryPlan
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show the index-metadata execution plan heuristic for a SELECT.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns Firebird's index-metadata-based execution plan heuristic for a single SELECT statement, listing which indexes exist on the tables it touches. Read-only, same restriction as firebird_runQuery. Use it to explain or optimize a slow query.

connectionId.description: A connection id returned by firebird_listConnections.

sql.description: A single SELECT statement to explain.

languageModelTools.name: firebird_runWriteQuery
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run a single INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE against a write-enabled Firebird connection.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Executes a single INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE against a Firebird connection that the user has explicitly write-enabled (see firebird_listConnections' writeEnabled field), granted from the connection's right-click menu in VS Code ('Toggle MCP Server Write Access'). Any other statement (SELECT/DDL/EXECUTE BLOCK) or more than one statement is rejected. The user is asked to confirm each call, and every attempt is logged. Only call this after the user has explicitly asked for a specific write, never speculatively.

connectionId.description: A connection id returned by firebird_listConnections.

sql.description: A single INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement.
